content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Washington, D.C.

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree and completion of project management education hours—no prior work experience needed. This makes the credential ideal for Washington professionals entering project management roles across federal, finance, nonprofit, and healthcare sectors. Verify your diploma or equivalent qualifies, then move forward.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Contact Hours of Education
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot camp. Our intensive course covers the PMBOK® Guide and exam domains, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend from anywhere; your cohort learns together in real time. Complete all sessions before submitting your PMI application.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing your education hours, apply directly to PMI with proof of your secondary degree and course completion. Pay the required examination fee. PMI processes applications within a standard timeframe; you'll receive authorization to schedule your exam once approved.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the CAPM Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides exam-preparation resources, practice questions, and study guidance to build your confidence. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center or take it online. Pass the exam to earn your CAPM credential—a recognized mark of project management competency.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Certification
steps_items.text: CAPM credentials renew every three years. Earn professional development units (PDUs) through project management training, conferences, or volunteer work. Plan your PDU strategy early to ensure continuous eligibility and stay current with evolving practices in your field.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.

fq_items.question: Is this training delivered online?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our CAPM training is fully live-virtual — no travel required. {city} students attend via video conference from wherever they are.

fq_items.question: Is CAPM certification worth it for project managers in Washington, DC?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Washington's economy relies on multi-year federal, nonprofit, and institutional programs where structured project methodology is expected. Employers like the World Bank Group, American Red Cross, and major universities prioritize certified credentials. CAPM demonstrates foundational PM knowledge and often serves as the stepping stone to PMP, positioning you for roles in the District's largest sectors—government, international development, healthcare, and higher education—where career growth and compensation typically accelerate with certification.
